# Table-ownership baseline (#2895) — per-(crate, table) count of NON-owner raw
# write sites (`INSERT [OR ...] INTO t` / `UPDATE t` / `DELETE FROM t`).
# Generated by: python3 scripts/check-table-ownership.py --update-baseline
# The check-table-ownership prek hook fails when a non-owner (crate, table)
# pair's count EXCEEDS its baseline. Owner-crate writes are unconstrained and
# never listed here. Ownership map: src-tauri/migrations/AGENTS.md.
#
# Format: <count> <crate> <table>  [# annotation]
# Blank lines and full-line `#` comments are ignored when parsing counts; an
# inline `# …` after the three fields documents WHY a cross-crate write is a
# sanctioned carve-out or WHEN it migrates. `--update-baseline` recomputes the
# counts but PRESERVES this header, every surviving pair's inline comment and
# the comment block directly above it (keyed by crate+table), and any footer.

# --- app crate: db/recovery.rs boot-time op-log replay/repair (maintainer
# carve-out 2026-07-24, #2895) — pre-engine, corrupt-DB-tolerant writers that
# cannot route through the engine projection (era-switched TEXT/INTEGER stamps,
# intentionally-divergent flat restore cohort #2043, page_id/reserved-column
# fixpoints). All 13 sites live in src/db/recovery.rs — the 13th is #4187's
# move-arm sweep, which cascade-soft-deletes a block a replayed `move_block`
# parked live under a tombstoned ancestor and is era-agnostic by construction
# (it copies the ancestor's stored `deleted_at` in SQL rather than binding an
# i64 the way the engine's `sweep_move_under_tombstoned_ancestor` does). ---
13 app blocks  # recovery carve-out: boot-time repair writes (pre-engine, corrupt-DB tolerant)

# --- engine crate: projection-time cache co-writers (legitimate carve-out,
# two-arm lockstep / sql_only fallback, #891) + op_log ingest (migrating) ---
2 engine agenda_cache  # projection co-writer (two-arm lockstep, #891)
2 engine block_links  # projection co-writer (two-arm lockstep, #891)
2 engine block_tag_inherited  # projection co-writer (two-arm lockstep, #891)
2 engine block_tag_refs  # projection co-writer (two-arm lockstep, #891)
2 engine page_link_cache  # projection co-writer (two-arm lockstep, #891)
4 engine pages_cache  # projection co-writer (two-arm lockstep, #891)
2 engine projected_agenda_cache  # projection co-writer (two-arm lockstep, #891)
2 engine tags_cache  # projection co-writer (two-arm lockstep, #891)

# === Split contract (maintainer-approved 2026-07-24, #2895) ===
# engine owns the Loro→SQL PROJECTION writes to `blocks`; store owns the
# PHYSICAL block primitives below it (page_id/space_id materialization,
# soft-delete, descendant cache) and cannot call up into engine. These 10
# store writers are sanctioned owner-adjacent carve-outs, not migratable debt.
10 store blocks  # owner-adjacent: physical primitives (split contract)

# --- sync crate: the snapshot RESET cache wipe (#3328). These seven writes
# are not new. `snapshot/restore.rs` has always truncated the store-owned
# derived caches before re-inserting a received snapshot's rows — it just did
# so through `format!("DELETE FROM {table}")`, which this guard's per-table
# literal regex cannot match, so the whole cross-crate wipe counted as ZERO
# and the sync crate had no line here at all. #3328 replaced the
# interpolation with a literal statement per table; the counts below are that
# pre-existing wipe becoming visible, not new debt.
#
# They stay cross-crate for now: the end-state (#2895 slice 4, already done
# for `block_links`) is an owner-side `truncate_all_caches` in
# agaric-store/src/cache/, at which point these seven lines drop to zero
# together. Until then, a NEW cache table wiped from here shows up as an
# eighth line and gets reviewed. ---
1 sync agenda_cache  # snapshot RESET wipe (#3328); migrates to an owner-side truncate helper
1 sync block_tag_inherited  # snapshot RESET wipe (#3328)
1 sync block_tag_refs  # snapshot RESET wipe (#3328)
1 sync page_link_cache  # snapshot RESET wipe (#3328)
1 sync pages_cache  # snapshot RESET wipe (#3328)
1 sync projected_agenda_cache  # snapshot RESET wipe (#3328)
1 sync tags_cache  # snapshot RESET wipe (#3328)
